item.title: Show HN: bouncemarket - a live prediction market game for a bouncing ball (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description:
a ball will fall. trade on where it lands.

I made this game! Some technical details:

The entire drop of the ball is simulated server-side, then streamed to each client as server-sent events with a small buffer. Every drop is deterministic from its starting position, so rounds can be replayed exactly for later analysis, but tiny variations in starting position can change the ultimate outcome.

There's some AI traders to keep the market moving, but they drop out in any round that has more than five people. They operate using a naive set of rules that I wrote for them, so they're not too hard to beat -- it's when the market is full of real people that it gets tricky.

Curious to get feedback on anything you would change, and especially whether the mechanics were clear right away or not.

item.title: Show HN: Pasteup - Paste screenshots into file upload fields (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description:
I'm currently a CS student, so that means a lot of file uploads to my university's janky website. I hated having to sort through the file picker just to attach an assignment open the next tab over. Pasteup is a Chrome extension that lets you press Cmd+V / Ctrl+V on the page instead, it finds the corresponding file box and attaches them automatically (if there are multiple it opens a picker).

Moreover I added an automatic file converter, so for things like CSV, txt, and code, it automatically converts it to the right format. This means my workflow went from going to the assignment sorting through 15 finder folders and uploading to ctrl a ctrl c ctrl v.

The file converter is pretty smart, and supports a lot of formats. If the field only takes PDF or JPG, it converts the file before uploading. It also turns copied spreadsheet cells into a CSV, JSON into a .json, and Figma's "Copy as SVG" into an image.

If you're already in any text boxes or editors it does nothing. If the site handles paste itself (FilePond, chat apps), it goes first, and Pasteup does nothing.

It runs entirely locally: no servers, no analytics, no network requests, no third-party libraries.

I'd love to hear about sites where it picks the wrong field or gets in the way or just any feedback in general!
